evidence.note: Real setup/payoff exchange: CPU lands 'Hall: Collar-and-elbow tie-up.' putting the player into GRAPPLED, and turn 9 offers a genuine choice between 'Grapple counter' (85%) and 'Break the grapple' (95%).

Best trade-off moment of the match - a two-option menu ('Kill the run' 87% reset vs 'Collision course' 87% pressure) resolves into 'Hitman snaps off collision course - Hall takes 16 damage.' with both wrestlers grounded.
Clear momentum swing for the CPU: 'Hall snaps off diving crossbody - Hitman takes 20 damage.' moves state from [130, 97] to [110, 97] and CPU momentum from 2 to 5.
Risk actually bites - the 62% Missile dropkick is reversed ('Hall reverses the missile dropkick - only 1 damage, and turns the tables!'), and the retry at turn 31 at 76% connects for 19.
Finish arrives with modest buildup rather than a climax: no near-fall in the match (near_fall_count 0) and the Sharpshooter wins on the first attempt from a grounded opponent at 77 HP.
Pin is visible the moment it is legal - the menu leads with 'Finish | Cover - pinfall attempt | pin | try to end it now; stronger when they're worn down' alongside the Sharpshooter.
The single-option turn is self-explaining rather than confusing: 'Fight to your feet' 95% with the note 'stand before they cover you; misses build escape momentum'.

Reversal chronology is a little thin - the log is only 'Hitman turns the tables!' for the CPU's 'Kill the run', with no statement of what was reversed or what changed; position stays TOP_ROPE / RUNNING_ROPES.

Submission labeling is ambiguous: 'Sharpshooter | 86% | cash in momentum for a match-ending swing' reads as an 86% chance to win. The 86% is the chance to apply the hold, and because the hold applied and Hall tapped immediately the display reinforces the misreading.

State changes are explained in plain language: 'Hitman snaps off missile dropkick - Hall takes 19 damage. / Hall is rattled - when they're forced up, big payoffs may open.' tells the player what the grounded state now unlocks.

stickiness.rematch_reason: The match was readable and moved through 12 distinct position pairings in 33 turns, and the turn-17 double-down and turn-22 crossbody comeback were genuinely interesting. But it ended on an unresisted first-attempt tap with zero near-falls, so the pull is mild curiosity rather than a need to run it back.
stickiness.next_experiment: Replay seed 227 taking the 'Cover - pinfall attempt' at turn 33 instead of the Sharpshooter to see whether the pin path produces the near-fall drama the submission path skipped, and try an aggressive policy that takes 'Springboard crossbody' at turn 7 and the grounded windows at turns 13 and 17 rather than resetting.

evidence.note: 'The crowd gasps - Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face.' is the kind of discovery moment that creates curiosity about what else can trigger.
The CPU's 20-damage diving crossbody shows the AI can actually punish a bad position, which makes a rematch feel non-trivial.
The tap-out comes on the first submission attempt with no escape drama, which blunts the finish and the appetite for an immediate rerun.
Standout narrative beat: 'Hitman snaps off collision course - Hall takes 16 damage. / The crowd gasps - Hall is busted open; blood streams down their face.'
Big spot with a matching state shift: 'Hall snaps off diving crossbody - Hitman takes 20 damage.' drops the player to GROUNDED and CPU momentum to 5.
Pre-finish tension is set up properly: 'Hall tries to rise but can't find it - still down and vulnerable to a cover!'

The finish uses a three-step delayed sequence (delays 1.0s, 1.5s, 0.0s) so the tap lands with pacing: 'Hitman hooks in sharpshooter! / Hall reaches for daylight... / The hold is cinched in deeper! / Hall taps out!'
Ceiling limited by drama density - near_fall_count 0 and 22 of 33 turns resolve as 'ok' positional lines with no damage.

top_issues.summary: Momentum saturates and stops being a decision. Player momentum hits 5 by turn 6 and sits at 5 through turn 28 while the CPU sits at 0 for the first 19 turns, so the resource that the loop tax is supposed to threaten has no headroom to matter here.

Submission percentage is presented as a bare 'Finish | Sharpshooter | 86%' with the note 'cash in momentum for a match-ending swing'. Nothing distinguishes apply-chance from win-chance, and the instant tap at turn 33 teaches the wrong lesson.
Zero near-falls and no failed submission attempt, so the match has no kickout or escape beat; the finish resolves on the first try.

The climb / pull-off-the-top exchange repeats at turns 25-26 and 27-28 with no anti-loop feedback of any kind. The loop tax appears to cover only the tie-up and grapple counter, so other neutral cycles get no 'losing steam' warning.
top_issues.suggested_area: game.py loop-tax coverage for climb and rope-running moves
